subject: ACME - Performance SLO/SLA follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: ACME call recap — perf targets & next steps

Hi John / Sara —

Thanks for a great conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side on performance / SLO topics so we can align on SLA language: 

Summary of ACME targets you mentioned:
- Latency: P95 <= 200ms for request sizes up to ~512 tokens (inference-only, streaming enabled)
- Throughput: sustained 100 QPS for batchless single-request traffic, able to spike to 150 QPS for short bursts
- Concurrency: support 50 concurrent sessions with active KV caches
- Streaming: server-side token streaming with first-byte latency < 120ms for streaming-enabled requests

Clarifying assumptions from Redwood:
- Latency targets measured server-side (Redwood gateway to final token flush) and reported as percentiles over 5-minute windows.
- Throughput and concurrency measured at the gateway accepted request rate, not client-side retries.
- Any required model variants/quantized profiles to meet these targets should be discussed during the tech deep dive.

Next steps:
1) I attached a first-pass SLA/SLO draft (ACME_Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf) with measurement definitions and proposed remedies. Please review the sections called "Latency measurement" and "Exclusions & maintenance".
2) Neha to schedule a technical workshop with ACME infra/ML infra team to validate load profile and streaming behavior (suggest Wed 10/22 or Thu 10/23).
3) If you agree to the measurement approach we can loop in Rishi for legal language on remedies/credits.

Anything missing from my summary? If this looks good I'll send calendar invites for the tech session.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: ACME_Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf (see sections: Latency measurement, Reporting cadence, Remedies)

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:02:13 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME call recap — perf targets & next steps

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifying questions before we dive into the tech workshop: 

1) When you say "server-side (gateway to final token flush)", does that include time spent queued when capacity is constrained (i.e., queue latency inside your routing layer), or is queueing excluded and counted as separate? We need clarity because our front-end will show end-to-end delays and we want a single reconciled view.

2) For P95 measurement windows, are you planning to use rolling 5-minute windows aggregated over 24h, or daily percentiles computed on 5-minute buckets? Spike handling matters for our alerts.

3) Streaming: we care about first-byte for streaming. If Redwood measures first-byte latency differently (e.g., after some server-side buffering), can you confirm you can provide both first-byte and end-of-stream metrics?

4) Remedies: our procurement requires a defined credit formula that is capped and tied to a reporting cadence. The draft's remedy language looks close but we need to confirm caps and escalation path.

We can proceed with the tech workshop, but please call out the expected measurement definitions in the doc (so legal has something concrete).

John
VP, Product
ACME Corp
john.doe@acme.com | +1 212-555-0147

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME call recap — perf targets & next steps

John — thanks, great questions. Answers below and notes on what we'll include in the updated draft prior to the tech session.

1) Queueing: Our standard SLO measurement includes end-to-end server-side time from gateway receipt to final token emission. That includes any server-side queuing (e.g., request waiting for GPU slot). We will add an explicit "queueing" metric in the reporting appendix so you can see queue contribution vs. pure inference time. If you prefer queueing excluded from the "latency SLO" we can offer an alternate SLO definition that uses "inference-only" time (request dequeued -> final token). We'll call this out as a configuration option.

2) Percentile windows: We compute percentiles on 5-minute rolling windows and report hourly/daily aggregates. For the SLA text we'll specify: "Reported P95 is the 95th percentile computed over five-minute rolling windows aggregated across the 24h period; any single five-minute window that fails the threshold may be escalated but credits are evaluated on the aggregated daily outcome." We'll add both the technical definition and an operational example in the appendix.

3) Streaming metrics: We will provide both first-byte (time from gateway receive to first token) and end-of-stream (time to final token) percentiles. For streaming requests we will also report the first-byte distribution and any rebuffer events.

4) Remedies / credits: In the draft we propose a graduated credit schedule (e.g., 5% credit for single-day breach up to X, 10% for multi-day sustained breach) with a hard cap equal to one month's service fee for the affected product. We can update the numbers to match ACME's procurement needs; please flag preferred caps in your review.

Attached is the SLA draft (same file) — I've highlighted the "Latency measurement" and "Remedies" sections. Neha will schedule the tech deep dive for Thu 10/23 at 10am PT (Calendar invite follows).

If that all looks good, I'll loop Rishi in to align on legal phrasing around escalation and remedies.

Best,
Marissa

Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ACME SLA language — please review remedies & exclusions

Rishi / Neha —

Looping you in as discussed. ACME requested clarity on:
- Whether queueing is included in the latency SLO (we've proposed including queueing by default and offering an "inference-only" alternate).
- Reporting cadence and exact percentile computation (we'll use 5-minute rolling windows aggregated for credits).
- Remedies: draft proposes graduated credits with a monthly cap (equal to one month's spend).

Ask: Can you please review the attached SLA draft and confirm whether the proposed remedies/cap language is acceptable from a legal/commercial perspective? Specific items to consider: 
- Is the "monthly cap = one month's affected product fee" acceptable, or do you want a different cap formula?
- Do we need to define audit rights / evidence timeline for ACME to dispute claimed breaches?
- Any redlines we should send before the tech workshop?

If possible, provide comments inline on the PDF (or share suggested redline text). I'm aiming to send an updated draft to ACME the morning of 10/23 so legal has time to review.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
